defend.name: Aegis Ward
defend.desc: After 3 hits: blocks the next incoming strike, then fades.

stun.name: Binding Hex
stun.desc: After 3 hits: stun foe for 2 seconds and remove 1 of their SP pips (if any).

avian.title: Avian Myth Line
avian.summary: Griffin → Hippogriff → Divine Griffon → Garuda or Phoenix → divine forms.

nodes.name: Griffin Hatchling
lore: A downy cross of eagle and lion, hatched where storm winds meet mountain stone.
Temple stories say the first griffins guarded gold and thunder before they ever served mortals.
Your myth begins small, but its wings already cast the shadow of a sky-bound throne.

nodes.name: Hippogriff
lore: Where Greek legend blended horse and raptor, the hippogriff became a mount of impossible speed.
It favors open air and honest wind—half pasture grace, half talon certainty.
In this line it marks the moment your beast leaves the nest for the long patrol of the clouds.

nodes.name: Divine Griffon
lore: The griffon here is no mere monster but a symbol of sacred vigil—beak, claws, and halo of rumor.
Chroniclers painted it on shields where gods watched borders men could not hold alone.
At this stage your myth carries weight: protector, omen, and claim upon the high places.

nodes.name: Garuda
lore: Garuda is the sun-bright foe of serpents, vehicle of Vishnu, wings wide as scripture.
Across Southeast Asian tale he tears through storm and scales to restore cosmic order.
Your Garuda answers the sea-roads: healing fury, sky-lit verdict on what coils below.

nodes.name: Divine Garuda
lore: Legends crown the king of birds in gold feathers and titles older than any single temple.
His cry is said to scatter eclipse and poison alike from the lands beneath his shadow.
As Divine Garuda, your myth finishes the ascent: not a pet but a living psalm above the waves.

nodes.name: Phoenix
lore: The phoenix gathers Greek fire-bird lore and Egypt’s solar bird of return into one burning arc.
It dies in ash only to rise, a metaphor every empire has tried to steal for itself.
Your Phoenix turns defeat into renewal—flame that mends as much as it consumes.

nodes.name: Eternal Phoenix
lore: Eternity here is not endless youth but endless cycle—each dusk a vow, each dawn a verdict.
Priests of sun and philosophers of becoming both wrote hymns to this singular ember.
Your Eternal Phoenix closes the Mediterranean branch: myth that outlives the map that named it.

serpent.title: Serpent / Dragon Line
serpent.summary: Naga line → Hydra, Orochi, Apophis, or Royal Nāga — legendaries per path.

nodes.name: Naga Hatchling
lore: Nāga hatchlings coil in monsoon lore—half spirit, half river, all appetite for growth.
Offerings at serpent shrines begin with scales no wider than a child’s hand.
Your myth’s first loop is already a promise of crowns, floods, and forbidden depths.

nodes.name: Greater Naga
lore: A Greater Naga commands eddies and respect from fishers who whisper rather than shout.
Temple murals stretch its body through whole jungles, each scale a boundary stone.
Sea influence swells its claim: guardian of straits, debtor to no single shore.

nodes.name: Mystic Serpent
lore: Neither dragon nor eel alone, the mystic serpent is omen inked on two oceans of story.
Greek and Japanese whispers braid here—Python’s smoke and river kami’s ripple.
At this fork your beast learns to stun fate itself, a heartbeat ahead of prophecy.

nodes.name: Hydra
lore: The Lernaean terror regrows heads when struck—Hera’s pet, heroes’ nightmare, math made flesh.
Its breath poisons the marsh; its defeat still costs a immortal hand in the tale.
Your Hydra embodies Greek chaos: every wound answered by more mouths to scream.

nodes.name: Lernaean Hydra
lore: Named for its fen, the Lernaean Hydra is the hydra perfected—regicide of hope itself.
Only fire and wit together tame it in myth; anything less feeds the neck-stump choir.
As legendary apex, your beast is the argument that some evils simply refuse to stay dead.

nodes.name: Orochi Fragment
lore: A shard of Yamata no Orochi recalls eight heads, eight hungers, and one doomed banquet.
Storm clouds and sakura both bend around the fragment’s wake.
Your Orochi Fragment binds foes in stun—the calm before Susanoo’s blade returns in story.

nodes.name: Yamata no Orochi
lore: The eight-headed dragon of Japanese myth drank rivers dry and demanded maidens yearly.
Its defeat birthed Kusanagi—proof that tyranny, however many mouths, can fall to one strike.
Your Yamata no Orochi is the full eclipse: stun made myth, storm given a spine.

nodes.name: Chaos Serpent
lore: Before Apophis earned a name, priests spoke of a chaos serpent gnawing at the sun-barge’s keel.
Lightning over the Nile was sometimes read as Ra’s spear repelling that coil.
Your Chaos Serpent attacks order itself—each strike a crack in the world’s noon.

nodes.name: Apophis
lore: Apophis is the undying foe of Ma’at—serpent of eclipse, entropy with fangs.
Every dawn in myth is a battle won against his squeeze on the solar barque.
Your Apophis ends the Egyptian branch in stun: the moment the sun hesitates and worlds hold their breath.

nodes.name: Royal Nāga
lore: Royal Nāgas wear crowns in mural and mantra, lords of monsoon treasury and monastic vow.
They bless rain and curse the proud who dredge rivers without leave.
Your Royal Nāga heals what the sea claims—salve written in scales and sutra.

nodes.name: Nāga King
lore: The Nāga King sits where mountain spring and ocean trench confess the same mother.
Legends seat him under Meru’s roots, defending dharma with fang and jewel.
Your Nāga King defends the line’s sea soul—threshold keeper between flood and throne.

trickster.title: Spirit Trickster Line
trickster.summary: Fox spirit → Kitsune → Elder Kitsune → nine-tails or Polong path.

nodes.name: Fox Spirit
lore: Fox spirits slip between farmstead and folktale, borrowing faces and returning favors in riddles.
A single tail still learns illusion—enough to stun a heart or a hunter’s aim.
Your Fox Spirit is the trickster’s first footprint: small, bright, and never quite where you looked.

nodes.name: Kitsune (3 tails)
lore: Three tails mark a kitsune stepping from curiosity into craft in Japanese lore.
Temple bells sometimes ring twice when such a fox passes—once for the world, once for the hidden.
Your three-tailed form binds foes longer; each tail is a lesson in patience and misdirection.

nodes.name: Elder Kitsune (5 tails)
lore: Five tails earn the title elder: old enough to guard shrines and young enough to test them.
Folklore ties greater tails to storms, weddings, and debts the living forget to pay.
Your Elder Kitsune raises wards—defense woven from smoke, oath, and borrowed moonlight.

nodes.name: 9-Tailed Kitsune
lore: Kyūbi no kitsune is apex fox—nine tails, centuries of hunger for wisdom or empire.
Some tales crown her ruin, others ascension; all agree she rewrites the board.
Your nine-tail strikes like rumor made blade: attack that lands before the truth catches up.

nodes.name: Celestial Kitsune
lore: Celestial kitsune tread constellations and ink-wash clouds, beyond province and season.
Monks paint them silver when mercy wins, gold when heaven needs a sharper envoy.
Your Celestial Kitsune ends the Japan path in starlit attack—trickster become aurora.

nodes.name: Polong Spirit Fox
lore: Polong is Malay spirit-lore: a fox-shaped haunt tied to blood, grudge, or broken taboo.
Shamans negotiate with such beings at thresholds of salt, iron, and whispered names.
Your Polong Spirit Fox defends through uneasy pact—ward raised where warm breath meets cold warning.

nodes.name: Shadow Trickster Deity
lore: At the sea line’s peak, trickster becomes deity—mask without a country, laugh without a throat.
Shadow pantheons love such gods: they keep courts honest and heroes humble.
Your Shadow Trickster Deity stuns fate’s chorus, the final line spoken from behind the curtain.

guardian.title: Guardian Beast Line
guardian.summary: Spirit hound → warden → Cerberus, Barong, or Anubis — each to a divine legendary.

nodes.name: Spirit Hound
lore: Spirit hounds haunt crossroads and hearths alike, baying at what flesh cannot see.
They are the first rank of guardians—loyal, hungry, and quick to drive intruders back.
Your Spirit Hound opens the line with honest attack: teeth before theology.

nodes.name: Guardian Beast
lore: A guardian beast is carved on tomb lintels and whispered into amulets against the restless dead.
Egyptian influence steels its purpose: watch the threshold, not the throne.
Your Guardian Beast raises defend—barrier born of vigil and funerary smoke.

nodes.name: Mythic Warden
lore: Wardens in myth judge who may pass—river, gate, or underworld ferry alike.
Greek and Egyptian law both loved a dog that would not flatter a king.
Your Mythic Warden stuns trespass mid-step, verdict before appeal.

nodes.name: Cerberus
lore: Cerberus keeps Hades’ door with three throats and one merciless welcome.
Orpheus charmed him; Heracles wrestled him—every myth agrees he cannot be bribed cheaply.
Your Cerberus defends the Greek branch: the ward no living army simply walks through.

nodes.name: Hades' Cerberus
lore: Hades’ own hound is titles and terror—pet of the rich man beneath the world.
His collar is sometimes peace, sometimes chain, depending on which poet survives copying.
Your Hades’ Cerberus is legendary defend: the last bark before oblivion’s accounting.

nodes.name: Barong
lore: Barong Ket dances Bali’s eternal fight—lion-leopard spirit against creeping destruction.
Drums and gilt mask turn village fear into communal courage each calendar of moons.
Your Barong heals through sacred uproar: mend the body while the crowd drives evil out.

nodes.name: Sacred Barong King
lore: The Sacred Barong King is procession and pact—when he rises, even kings step aside.
His crown is parasol, fang, and laughter braided into law older than codex.
Your Sacred Barong King heals at mythic scale: blessing that stitches village to cosmos.

nodes.name: Anubis Beast
lore: Anubis guides scales and shrouds—the jackal face of embalming and honest weight.
His beast form prowls necropolis sand where stars copy the geometry of judgment.
Your Anubis Beast heals what the rites begin: breath returned where the heart is light.

nodes.name: Divine Anubis
lore: Divine Anubis is no longer merely guide but verdict walking on four silent paws.
Scales shine; the feather waits; the duat holds its breath for your myth’s name.
Your Divine Anubis defends the Egyptian apex—law incarnate, mercy armored in obsidian.
